This is third application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of the Cr.P.C., 1973) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.511/2023, dated 10.11.2023 registered at Police Station- Athner, District-Betul (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Applicant is in detention since 21.11.2023.
2.
Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 02.08.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.23823 of 2024.
His second bail application was disposed of with liberty to revive the prayer for grant of bail after receipt of DNA report vide order dated 24.09.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.41251 of 2024.

3. As per the prosecution story, on 10.11.2023, 16 years & one month old prosecutrix, a student of Class - XII, lodged an FIR stating that she knew NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1274 2 MCRC-54831-2024 Neelesh Bele (present applicant) for the last more than one year and they were on talking terms. On 27.05.2023, Neelesh called her outside of the village at Bhojudena Jod; at this,
she went to meet him.

He told that he likes her and wanted to marry with her and on the false promise of marriage committed rape upon her and thereafter, he again committed rape upon her,
due to which, she conceived.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge- sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is in detention since 21.11.2023.
He has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.

Proseutrix &
applicant who are almost of the same age group were having love affairs with each-other.

Prosecutrix on her own had gone with the applicant and they were having romantic love relationship and had consensually established physical relations and on account of relationship, prosecutrix conceived and delivered a child.
Prosecutrix was a consenting party.
It is a case of romantic love relationship.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix has already been examined before the Trial Court and according to her, she was having consensual physical relation with the applicant.
Final conclusion of trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail, pending the trial.
5 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.1/State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
6. As per DNA report, applicant has been found the biological father of the child delivered by the prosecutrix.

Prosecutrix and her parents have NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1274 3 MCRC-54831-2024 already been examined before the Trial Court and now, there is no possibility of influencing of prosecution witnesses and tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Applicant is in jail for the last more than one year.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts &
circumstances of the case including the fact that final conclusion of trial of the case will take considerable time, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of the Cr.P.C., 1973) for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7 . It is directed that applicant - Neelesh be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023 [Section 437(3) of CrPC].
8 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1274 4 MCRC-54831-2024 @shish Neelesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191605459/
